findings.issue_text: [BUG] This diff deletes the public symbols mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context, and SimpleCheckIn from mark_failed.py without updating any other in-repo call sites shown in the diff. Any existing module or test importing mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, or SimpleCheckIn from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (the pre-refactor locations) now raises ImportError at import time, breaking those callers and CI even though mark_failed's own behavior is unchanged.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes a `config` copy with schedule_type converted to its human display value but then returns the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`, discarding the conversion. The monitor context serialized into every incident occurrence's event_data carries schedule_type as the raw integer enum instead of the display string, so the issue UI renders a numeric schedule type for users; the conversion code is dead and the next editor of this function will not notice the returned value bypasses it.

[ADVISORY] The ERROR-state path builds previous_checkins as a one-element list of the current failed checkin and then loops a DB re-fetch over it, hiding that the loop is effectively single-iteration and duplicating a query for the row already in hand as failed_checkin. The loop re-fetches full MonitorCheckIn rows by id just to call create_incident_occurrence once per checkin, but every call passes the same `previous_checkins` list and produces an occurrence differing only by trace_id; when a threshold of N is first crossed in the OK->ERROR branch, N near-identical Kafka occurrences are produced for one incident, and consumers of this refactor cannot verify from the diff that the occurrence-fanout behavior was intended to be preserved because no test in the diff pins the occurrence count.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context copies the monitor config and rewrites schedule_type into the local `config` variable but then returns the untouched `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, discarding the computed display value. The monitor context emitted in every incident occurrence event_data carries the raw machine schedule_type (e.g. "crontab") instead of the human-readable display value the code was written to produce; users inspecting event context see the internal enum, and the copy/rewrite block is dead code that misleads the next maintainer into thinking display conversion happens.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes and mutates a `config` local (replacing schedule_type with its display value) but then returns the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead, so the schedule_type display substitution is dead code and never reaches the occurrence payload. Downstream issue-creation consumers receive the raw integer schedule_type in the monitor context instead of the intended human-readable display string; every user-facing occurrence for scheduled monitors shows a numeric schedule type, and the next editor of this function will believe the display conversion is applied when it is not.

[ADVISORY] try_incident_threshold loops over every check-in in the threshold window and produces one full IssueOccurrence to Kafka per check-in for a single incident transition. For a threshold of N, one failed check-in emits N near-identical occurrences (same fingerprint, same incident) to Kafka and the issue platform; with large failure_issue_threshold values this multiplies producer load and creates duplicate evidence events per incident. The strongest counterargument is that the fingerprint dedupes them into one group, so only the first matters; but the fan-out still costs N Kafka produces and N consumer-side processing for one logical state change, and only the first check-in's trace_id carries meaningful evidence.

[ADVISORY] get_failure_reason filters failed check-ins to statuses in HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, so when every check-in's status is outside that map (e.g. a future/unknown status), status_counts is empty and the function returns ' check-ins detected' with a blank list, and its docstring examples ('3 missed check-ins detected') do not match the actual output format ('3 missed check-ins check-ins detected'). A caller introducing a new CheckInStatus that fires mark_failed but is not added to the map gets an empty failure-reason string in user-facing evidence, and the docstring misleads the next maintainer about the produced string. Counterargument: all current failure statuses are covered; but the map-lookup is the single hand-maintained enumeration gating the output, so any new status silently degrades evidence rather than failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds a local `config` copy with the humanized `schedule_type` display value but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` verbatim, so the computed `config` is dead code and the monitor context always carries the raw integer schedule_type. Anyone reading the monitor issue context (JSON evidence in the issue platform payload) gets the raw schedule_type int instead of the display string the code clearly intends; the bug was carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py into the new file during this move, and every future reader of the 'new' module will re-trip over the misleading copy-vs-return structure.

[ADVISORY] SimpleCheckIn (along with get_failure_reason, HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, and get_monitor_environment_context) was moved out of sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py to new modules with no re-export shim left behind, so any in-tree or plugin caller importing these symbols from the old path now fails with ImportError at import time. Test modules and any out-of-tree consumers that imported `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import SimpleCheckIn` (the symbol's only home before this diff) break on upgrade; if this refactor was accepted as a pure reorganization without an explicit decision about the import surface, the objective silently changed from 'reorganize' to 'reorganize plus API removal'.

[ADVISORY] try_incident_threshold is a byte-for-byte behavioral clone of the removed mark_failed_threshold, meaning the refactor is behavior-preserving, but it also preserves the known race where two concurrent failing check-ins can both pass the `monitor_env.status in [OK, ACTIVE]` check (the status read happens before `refresh_from_db` in the caller) and each fire an occurrence loop, so the 'reorganize' objective cannot be closed out without an explicit human acceptance that the duplicated-occurrence behavior is unchanged-and-accepted. Reviewers evaluating this PR as a pure move will miss that the preserved double-fire path (one occurrence per check-in in the id__in loop, up to threshold occurrences per failing check-in) is now the canonical implementation in two new modules rather than one obvious location, making the next behavior change harder and the original acceptance criteria (incident-per-threshold) implicitly re-ratified without sign-off.

[BUG] The refactor removes the exported symbols mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context, HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP, and SimpleCheckIn from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed with no test-file modifications in this diff, so the existing monitor test suite (e.g. tests/sentry/monitors/test_mark_failed.py, which imports and calls mark_failed_threshold/create_issue_platform_occurrence directly per the pre-refactor API) now fails at import time with ImportError, meaning the moved incident-threshold and occurrence logic in incidents.py/incident_occurrence.py is exercised by zero tests. CI on the monitors test modules errors with ImportError before any assertion runs, and the new logic/incidents.py + logic/incident_occurrence.py code paths (threshold gating, get_or_create incident, muted checks, kafka produce) have no test coverage keyed to their new locations; I checked the diff for any test-shaped file (*.test.*, *_test.py, tests/**) referencing try_incident_threshold, create_incident_occurrence, or the new modules and found none, so the absence is of test-file changes entirely.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes a transformed `config` copy (with schedule_type converted to its display string) but then discards it, embedding the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in the returned context. The monitor context attached to every incident occurrence event carries the raw numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable display value the copy/transform was written to produce, so users see an opaque integer in the issue UI; the dead `config = ...copy()` lines also make the next change to this context riskier. (Carried over from the original mark_failed.py but now permanently enshrined in the new module this diff creates.)

This means a single incident transition can emit up to N near-identical occurrences (same `fingerprint=[incident.grouphash]`, same incident tag), increasing Kafka/consumer load and duplicating occurrences; this is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior, but is more of a performance/duplication concern than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `get_failure_reason` (new `incident_occurrence.py`), the Counter only includes statuses present in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`. If none match, `status_counts` is empty, `get_text_list([])` will yield an empty string, and the function returns a user-facing string like `" check-ins detected"` (blank reason). That’s a real edge-case robustness issue tied to the hand-maintained map. However, the finding’s claim that the normal output becomes `"3 missed check-ins check-ins detected"` is not supported by the code: `human_status` is built as `"%(count)d %(status)s"` (e.g. `"3 missed"`), so the final string is `"3 missed check-ins detected"`, which matches the docstring example.

As a result, any code that previously imported these symbols from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` would now raise `ImportError`. The diff alone can’t confirm whether any in-tree or external consumers rely on the old import path, but the breaking change in import surface is real and review-relevant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `try_incident_threshold` is effectively the moved/renamed logic from `mark_failed_threshold` (same status branching, same `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)`, and same loop over `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=...)` calling `create_incident_occurrence`). There is no locking (`select_for_update`, atomic update, etc.) around the `monitor_env.status in [OK, ACTIVE]` check + subsequent `monitor_env.status = ERROR; save()`, so concurrent workers could still both take the OK/ACTIVE branch and both emit occurrences; the occurrence loop can also emit multiple occurrences (one per checkin id in `previous_checkins`). However, the finding’s specific claim that the status read happens before `refresh_from_db` in the caller is not supported by the diff (the caller still does `monitor_env.refresh_from_db()` before calling `try_incident_threshold`). Overall this is a diff-grounded architectural/behavior-preservation concern rather than a new, verifiable defect introduced here.
